volume: 第九卷貪吝部 Volume 9: Greed and Stinginess Department

stories.text: 有慕開典鋪者，謀之人曰：「需本幾何？」曰：「大典萬金，小者亦須千計。」其人大駭而去。更請一人問之，曰：「百金開一錢當亦可。」又辭去。最後一人曰：「開典如何要本錢，只須店櫃一張，當票數紙足矣。」此人乃欣然。擇期開典，至日，有持物來當者，驗收訖，填空票計之。當者索銀，答曰：「省得稱來稱去，費壞許多手腳，待你取贖時，只將利銀來交便了。」
stories.translation: A person named Kaidianpu asked, "What is the principal required?" He said, "For a major loan, ten thousand gold coins are needed; even for smaller ones, at least thousands are required." The person was greatly startled and left. He then asked another person, who said, "Opening a pawn with one coin for every hundred coins is also possible." The person declined and left again. Finally, another person said, "Opening a pawn shop does not require capital; one only needs a single counter and several pawn tickets." This person was delighted. He chose a date to open the pawn shop, and on that day, someone came with items to be pawned. After inspecting and accepting them, he filled out blank tickets as records. When the pawn customer asked for silver, he replied, "It is troublesome to weigh and measure repeatedly, which wastes a lot of effort. When you come to redeem it later, just bring the interest in silver."

stories.text: 一吝者，家有禱事，命道士請神，乃通城請兩京神道。主人曰：「如何請這遠的？」道士答曰：「近處都曉得你的情性，說請他，他也不信。」
stories.translation: A stingy man, whose family had a religious ceremony, ordered a Taoist priest to summon deities. He summoned two deities from the capital cities of Tongcheng. The host asked, "Why invite someone so far away?" The Taoist priest replied, "Those nearby all know your character; if we say we are inviting him, he won't believe it."

stories.text: 一人好放債，家已貧矣，止餘斗粟，仍謀煮粥放之。人問「如何起利？」答曰：「討飯。」
stories.translation: A man enjoyed lending money. His family had already become poor, with only a single measure of grain left, yet he still planned to cook porridge and lend it out. Someone asked, "How will you generate interest?" He replied, "By begging for food."

stories.text: 好善者曰：「聞當日佛好慈悲，曾割肉喂鷹，投崖喂虎。我欲效之，但鷹在天上，虎在山中，身上有肉，不能使啖，夏天蚊子甚多，不如捨身齋了蚊罷。」乃不掛帳，以血飼蚊。佛欲試其虔誠，變一虎啖之。其人大叫曰：「小意思吃些則可，若認真這樣大東道，如何當得起！」
stories.translation: A kind-hearted person said, "I have heard that in ancient times the Buddha was very compassionate. He once cut his flesh to feed an eagle and threw himself off a cliff to feed a tiger." "I wish to emulate him, but eagles are in the sky and tigers are in the mountains. Though I have flesh on my body, they cannot eat it. There are many mosquitoes in summer; it would be better if I offer myself as a meal for these mosquitoes." He therefore did not hang mosquito nets and used his blood to feed the mosquitoes. The Buddha, wishing to test his sincerity, transformed into a tiger to devour him. The man cried out in alarm, "A little taste is fine, but if you really go through with such a grand gesture, how could I possibly bear it!"

stories.text: 一人性最貪，富者語之曰：「我白送你一千銀子，你與我打死了罷。」其人沉吟良久，曰：「只打半死，與我五百兩何如？」
stories.translation: A man was extremely greedy. A wealthy person told him, "I will give you one thousand silver coins for free; just agree to let me beat you to death." The man hesitated for a long time and said, "How about if I am only beaten half to death, you give me five hundred taels instead?"

stories.text: 鄉下親家新製佳釀，城裏親家慕而訪之，冀其留飲。適親家他往，親母命子款待，權為荒榻留宿。其親母臥房止隔一壁，親家因未得好酒到口，方在懊悶。值親母桶上撤尿，恐聲響不雅，努力將臀夾緊，徐徐滴瀝而下。親家聽見，私自喜曰：「原來才在裡面濾酒哩，想明早得嘗其味矣。」親母聞言，不覺失笑，下邊鬆動，尿聲急大。親家拍掌嘆息曰：「真是命窮，可惜濾酒榨袋，又撐破了。」
stories.translation: A country in-law had recently brewed fine wine. The city in-law, envious and admiring it, visited to inquire, hoping he would be invited to stay for a drink. Just then the in-law was away. The mother-in-law ordered her son to entertain him, and temporarily offered an empty bed for lodging. The mother-in-law's bedroom was only separated by a wall, and the in-law, having not yet tasted the good wine, felt annoyed. Just then, the mother-in-law was urinating in a chamber pot. Afraid that the sound would be impolite, she strained to clench her buttocks tightly and let it drip slowly down. The in-law heard this, secretly happy, saying, "So the wine is being filtered inside; I suppose I will get to taste it tomorrow morning." The mother-in-law heard this and couldn't help but laugh, causing her lower body to relax slightly, making the urine flow suddenly louder. The in-law clapped his hands and sighed, saying, "Truly a life of poverty; unfortunately, the wine press bag broke again."

stories.text: 有兄弟合種田者，禾既熟。議分。兄謂弟曰：「我取上截，你取下截。」弟訝其不平，兄曰：「不難，待明年你取上，我取下可也。」至次年，弟催兄下穀種，兄曰：「我今年意欲種芋頭哩。」
stories.translation: There were brothers who farmed together, and their crops had matured. They discussed dividing them. The older brother said to his younger brother, "I will take the upper part; you take the lower part." The younger brother was surprised at this being unfair. The older brother said, "It's not difficult; next year you can take the upper part and I will take the lower one." łoż The following year, the younger brother urged his older brother to sow the grain. The older brother replied, "I have decided this year to plant taro instead."

stories.text: 甲乙謀合本做酒，甲謂乙曰：「汝出米，我出水。」乙曰：「米若我的，如何算帳？」甲曰：「我決不虧心。到酒熟時，只逼還我這些水罷了，其餘多是你的。」
stories.translation: Jia and Yi planned to partner in brewing wine. Jia said to Yi, "You provide the rice; I will provide the water." Yi asked, "If the rice is mine, how should we account for it?" Jia said, "I will certainly not be unfair. When the wine is ready, I'll just ask you to repay me for this water; everything else will belong to you."

stories.text: 窮人暑月無帳，復惜蚊煙費，忍熱擁被而臥，蚊囋其面。鄰家有一鬼臉，借而帶之。蚊口不能入，謂曰：「汝不過省得一文錢耳，如何便翻了臉？」
stories.translation: A poor man, lacking mosquito nets in the hot summer months and unwilling to spend money on mosquito coils, endured the heat by hugging his quilt while mosquitoes bit his face. A neighbor had a ghost mask; he borrowed it and wore it. The mosquitoes could not bite through the mask, so they said, "You only saved one coin; how can you turn your face like this?"

stories.text: 一人要寫行樂圖，連紙筆顏料，共送銀二分。畫者乃用水墨于荊川紙上，畫出一背像。其人怒曰：「寫真全在容顏，如何寫背？」畫者曰：「我勸你莫把面孔見人罷。」
stories.translation: A man wanted to have a portrait painted, and he gave two coins in total for the paper, brushes, and pigments. The painter used ink on Jingchuan paper to draw a portrait from behind. The man became angry and said, "A true portrait must capture the face; why did you paint only the back?" The painter replied, "I suggest you not show your face to people after all."

stories.text: 一人性極吝嗇，從無請客之事。家僮偶持碗一籃，往河邊洗滌，或問曰：「你家今日莫非宴客耶？」僮曰：「要我家主人請客，除非那世裡去！」主人知而罵曰：「誰要你輕易許下他日子！」
stories.translation: A man was extremely stingy and had never hosted a guest. lington The servant happened to carry a basket of bowls to the riverbank for washing, and someone asked, "Is your master having guests over today?" The servant replied, "Unless we go to the other world, my master will never host a guest!" Upon hearing this, the master scolded and said, "Who asked you to casually promise him that day?"

stories.text: 有人遇喜事，一友封分金一星往賀，乃密書對內云：「現五分，賒五分。」己而此友亦有賀分，其人仍以一星之敬答之。乃以空封往，內書云：「退五分，賒五分。」
stories.translation: A man had a happy occasion, and one friend sent a small gift of a single star coin to congratulate him. However, he secretly wrote on the envelope: "Five cents in cash, five cents on credit." Later, when this friend also had a celebration and sent a gift, the man still responded with only one star coin as his offering. He sent an empty envelope instead, writing inside: "Return five cents, credit five cents."

stories.text: 有夜飲者，僕攜燈往候，主曰：「少時天便明，何用燈為？」僕乃歸。至天明，僕復往接，主責曰：「汝大不曉事，今日反不帶燈來，少頃就是黃昏，叫我如何回去？」
stories.translation: A man who was drinking at night had his servant carry a lamp to wait for him. The master said, "In a little while it will be daylight; why do you need the lamp?" The servant then returned home. When it became daylight, the servant went back to meet him. The master scolded, "You are very unwise; you didn't bring a lamp today. In a moment it will be dusk again—how am I supposed to go home?"

stories.text: 客遠來久坐，主家雞鴨滿庭，乃辭以家中乏物，不敢留飯。客即借刀，欲殺己所乘馬治餐。主曰：「公如何回去？」客曰：「憑公於雞鴨中，告借一隻，我騎去便了。」
stories.translation: A guest had come from afar and sat for a long time. The host's courtyard was full of chickens and ducks, yet he excused himself by saying there were no supplies at home and dared not offer a meal. The guest immediately asked to borrow a knife, intending to kill the horse he had ridden for food. The host said, "How will you go back?" The guest replied, "Please let me borrow one of your chickens or ducks; I will ride it back."

stories.text: 一客坐至晌午，主絕無留飯之意。適聞雞聲，客謂主曰：「晝雞啼矣。」主曰：「此客雞不準。」客曰：「我肚飢是準的。」
stories.translation: A guest sat until midday, but the host showed no intention of offering him a meal. Just then they heard a rooster crowing; the guest said to the host, "The daytime rooster is crowing." The host replied, "This is not an accurate chicken of ours." The guest said, "My hungry stomach is definitely real."

stories.text: 一人為虎銜去，其子執弓逐之，引滿欲射。父從虎口遙謂其子曰：「我兒須是兜腳射來，不要傷壞了虎皮，沒人肯出價錢。」
stories.translation: A man was carried off by a tiger. His son took up a bow and chased after it, drawing the string back to shoot. From the tiger's mouth, the father called out to his son from afar, "My son must shoot at its legs. Don't damage the tiger skin; otherwise, no one will pay for it."

stories.text: 一人遠出回家，對妻云：「我到燕子磯，蚊蟲大如雞。後過三山硤，蚊蟲大如鴨。昨在上新河，蚊蟲大如鵝。」妻云：「呆子，為甚不帶幾隻回來吃。」夫笑曰：「他不吃我就夠了，你還敢想去吃他！」
stories.translation: A man returned home from a distant journey and said to his wife, "When I arrived at Yanziji, the mosquitoes there were as big as chickens. Later, when I passed Sanshan Jia, the mosquitoes were as large as ducks." "Yesterday at Shangxinhe, the mosquitoes were even as big as geese." His wife said, "Fool, why didn't you bring a few back to eat?" The husband laughed and said, "They don't even want to eat me; how dare you think of eating them!"

stories.text: 一人性最慳吝，忽感癆瘵之疾，醫生診視云：「脈氣虛弱，宜用人參培補。」病者驚視曰：「力量綿薄，惟有委命聽天可也。」醫士曰：「參既不用，須以熟地代之，其價頗賤。」病者搖首曰：「費亦太過，願死而已。」醫知其吝嗇，乃詐言曰：「別有一方，用乾狗屎調黑糖一二文服之，亦可以補元神。」病者躍然起問曰：「不知狗屎一味，可以禿用否？」
stories.translation: A man was extremely stingy. One day he suddenly fell ill with consumption, and a doctor examined him and said, "Your pulse is weak; you should take ginseng to strengthen your constitution." The patient looked up in alarm and said, "My strength is weak; I can only leave my fate to heaven." The doctor said, "If you won't take ginseng, then at least use Shu Di as a substitute; it is relatively cheap." The patient shook his head and said, "Even that cost is too high. I would rather die." Knowing the man's stinginess, the doctor lied and said, "There is another prescription; take one or two coins' worth of dried dog dung mixed with black sugar. It can also replenish your vital energy." The patient jumped up and asked excitedly, "I wonder if this dried dog dung can be used in a shaved amount?"

stories.text: 一人做粉孩兒出賣，生意甚好，謂妻曰：「此後只做束手的，粉可稍省。」果賣去。又曰：「此後做坐倒的，當更省。」仍賣去。乃曰：「如今做垂頭而臥者，不更省乎！」及做就，妻提起看曰：「省則省矣，只是看看不像個人了。」
stories.translation: A man made powdered children for sale, and his business was very successful. He told his wife, "From now on, I will only make those with their hands tied; this way, we can save a little powder." And indeed he sold them. He then said, "From now on I will make the ones sitting down; this should save even more." And he sold them again. He then said, "Now I will make those lying down with their heads hanging; won't that save even more?" When they were made, the wife picked one up and looked at it, saying, "It does save some, but now it doesn't even look like a person anymore."

stories.text: 一人謀做褲而吝布，連喚裁縫，俱以費布辭去。最後一縫匠云：「只須三尺足矣。」其人大喜，買布與之。乃縫一腳管，令穿兩足在內。其人曰：「迫甚，如何行得？」縫匠曰：「你脫煞要省，自然一步也行不開的。」
stories.translation: A man wanted to make pants but was stingy with the cloth, and repeatedly called in tailors, who all refused because it would cost too much fabric. The last tailor said, "Only three chi will be enough." The man was very pleased and bought the cloth for him. He then sewed one leg tube, telling him to put both feet inside it. The man said, "It's too tight; how can I possibly walk in this?" The tailor said, "You wanted to save as much as possible. Naturally, you won't be able to take a single step."

stories.text: 一人性吝者，買布一丈，命裁縫要做馬衣一件，褲一條，襪一雙，餘布還要做頂包巾。匠每以布少辭去。落後一裁縫曰：「我做只消八尺，倒與你省卻兩尺，何如？」其人大喜。縫者竟做成一長袋，將此人從腳套至頭頂，口用繩收緊。其人曰：「氣悶極矣。」匠曰：「撞著你這慳吝鬼，自然是氣悶的。省是省了，要想出頭，卻難哩。」
stories.translation: A man who was very stingy bought one zhang of cloth and ordered the tailor to make a horse coat, a pair of pants, a pair of socks, and still have enough left over to make a headscarf. Each time the tailor refused because there was not enough cloth. Finally, one tailor said, "I can make it with only eight chi; I will actually save you two chi. How does that sound?" The man was overjoyed. The tailor actually made a long bag, putting the man from his feet up to the top of his head, and tied it shut with a rope at the opening. The man said, "It's suffocating!" The tailor said, "Meeting a miser like you, it's naturally going to be suffocating." We did save on the cloth. But if you want to stick your head out, it's going to be hard."

stories.title_en: Not a Single Hair Will Be Plucked
stories.text: 一猴死見冥王，求轉人身。王曰：「既欲做人，須將身上毛盡行拔去。」即喚夜叉動手。方拔一根，猴不勝痛楚，王笑曰：「畜生，看你一毛不拔，如何做人！」
stories.translation: A monkey died and appeared before the King of Hell, begging to be reborn as a human. The king said, "If you wish to become a person, you must pull out all the hair on your body." He immediately called for a night demon to do it. Just as they pulled out one hair, the monkey could not bear the pain. The king laughed and said, "Beast, look at you—refusing to part with even a single hair. How can you become a person!"

stories.title_en: Losing the Forest for the Trees
stories.text: 有造方便覓利者，遙見一人撩衣，知必小解，恐其往所對鄰廁，乃偽為出恭，而先踞其上。小解者果赴己廁。其人不覺，偶撒一屁，帶下糞來，乃大悔恨，曰：「何苦因小失大。」
stories.translation: There was a man who sought profit by providing convenience. From afar, he saw someone lifting his clothes, knowing that the person must be about to urinate. Fearing that this person would go to the adjacent latrine, he pretended to need to relieve himself and took up position there first. The man who wanted to urinate indeed went to his latrine. The man did not notice, and accidentally let out a fart that brought down some feces. He was greatly regretful and said, "Why must I lose the big thing for such a small gain?"

stories.text: 一家延師，供饌甚薄。一日，賓主同坐，見籬邊一雞，指問主人曰：「雞有幾德？」主曰：「五德。」師曰：「以我看來，雞有七德。」問：「為何多了二德？」答曰：「我便吃得，你卻捨不得。」
stories.translation: A family hired a teacher, but provided very meager meals. One day, the guest and host were sitting together when they saw a chicken by the fence. The guest pointed at it and asked the owner, "How many virtues does a chicken have?" The host said, "Five virtues." The teacher said, "In my view, a chicken has seven virtues." Asked, "Why are there two more virtues?" The answer was, "I can eat it, but you won't let me."

stories.text: 東家供師甚薄，久不買葷。一日，糞缸內淹死一雞，烹以為饌。師食而疑之，問其徒，徒以實告，師憤甚。少頃，主人進館，師忙執笤帚二把，塞其口中，逼使盡食。東家曰：「笤帚如何吃得？」師曰：「你既不肯吃笤帚，如何倒叫先生吃糞雞（箕）。」
stories.translation: The host provided very poor food for his teacher and had not bought any meat for a long time. One day, a chicken drowned in the latrine pit; they cooked it as food. The teacher ate it and suspected something was wrong. He asked his student, who told him the truth, which greatly angered the teacher. A short while later, when the host came into the study hall, the teacher hurriedly took two brooms and stuffed them into his mouth, forcing him to eat them all. The host said, "How can one possibly eat a broom?" The teacher said, "If you are unwilling to eat the broom, how can you make your teacher eat a chicken that drowned in feces (literally 'fecal chicken')?"

stories.text: 一神道險惡，賽者必用生人祭禱。有酬願者，苦乏人獻，特於供桌中挖一孔，藏身在桌下，而伸頭於桌面。俟神舉箸，頭忽縮下。神大怒，罵曰：「這班小鬼都是賊，才得舉箸，如何嗄飯就一些沒有了。」
stories.translation: An evil deity, whose shrine demanded the sacrifice of a living person for any contest. One who wished to fulfill this vow, but was troubled by the lack of people to sacrifice, specially dug a hole in the altar table and hid himself underneath it, extending only his head onto the tabletop. He waited until the deity picked up chopsticks; at that moment, he suddenly pulled his head down. The deity became very angry and scolded, saying, "These little devils are all thieves. Just as I picked up the chopsticks, how come there is already not a single grain of rice left?"

stories.text: 二子午餐，問父用何物下飯，父曰：「古人望梅止渴，可將壁上掛的腌魚望一望，吃一口，這就是下飯了。」二子依法行之。忽小者叫云：「阿哥多看了一眼。」父曰：「咸殺了他。」
stories.translation: Two sons were having lunch and asked their father what he used to accompany his rice. The father said, "The ancients quenched their thirst by merely looking at plums; you can look at the salted fish hanging on the wall for a moment, take one bite, and that will be enough as an accompaniment to your rice." The two sons followed his method. Suddenly, the younger one shouted, "Big brother took an extra look." The father said, "He's been salted to death."

stories.text: 有擔榧子在街賣者，一人連吃不止。賣者曰：「你買不買，如何只管吃？」答曰：「此物最能養脾。」賣者曰：「你雖養脾，我卻傷心。」
stories.translation: A man was selling walnuts on the street, and another person kept eating them without stopping. The seller said, "Will you buy or not? Why are you just eating continuously?" He replied, "This thing is best for nourishing the spleen." user

stories.text: 一先生開館，東家設宴相待，以其初到加禮，乃宰一鵝奉款。飲至酒闌，先生謂東翁曰：「學生取擾的日子正長，以後飲饌．毋須從儉，庶得相安。」因指盤中鵝曰：「日日只此一味足矣，其餘不必羅列。」
stories.translation: A teacher opened a school, and the host held a banquet to entertain him. Because it was his first day there, they treated him with extra courtesy by slaughtering a goose as an offering of hospitality. As the banquet was drawing to a close, the teacher said to his host, "Since I will be staying here for quite some time, in the future there is no need to be too frugal with food and drink. This way we can live in peace." He then pointed at the goose on the plate and said, "Every day just this one dish is enough; there's no need to prepare anything else."

stories.text: 有為兒孫作馬牛者，臨終之日，呼諸子而問曰：「我死後，汝輩當如何殯殮？」長子曰：「仰體大人惜費之心，不敢從厚，縞衣布衾，二寸之棺，一寸之槨，墓道僅以土封。」翁攢眉良久，責其多費。次子曰：「衣衾棺槨，俱不敢用，但具蒿薦一條，送於郊外，謂之火葬而已。」翁猶疾其過奢。三子嘿喻父意，乃詭詞以應曰：「吾父愛子之心，無所不至，既經殫力於生前，並惜捐軀於死後？不若以大人遺體，三股均分，暫作一日之屠兒，以享百年之遺澤，何等不好？」翁乃大笑曰：「吾兒此語，適獲我心。」復戒之曰：「對門王三老，慣賴肉錢，斷斷不可賒。」
stories.translation: There was a man who had worked like a horse and ox for his children and grandchildren. On the day of his death, he called his sons and asked them, "After I die, how should you bury me?" The eldest son said, "We will follow your wish to save expenses and not go for an extravagant funeral. We'll use plain hemp clothes and a coarse cloth shroud, a two-cun coffin, and one cun outer case. The tomb path will be sealed only with earth." The old man furrowed his brows for a long time and scolded them for the expense. The second son said, "We won't use any clothes, shroud, coffin or outer case at all. We will just prepare a single mat of wormwood and send you to the outskirts for cremation." The old man still considered it too extravagant. The third son silently understood his father's intention and replied with a fabricated statement, saying, "My father's love for us children is boundless. If he has already exhausted all efforts in life, why would he not be willing to give up his body after death?" "Why not divide your father's remains into three equal parts and temporarily act as butchers for a day, to enjoy the blessings of his legacy for a hundred years? How could that be bad?" The old man then laughed heartily and said, "My son's words have perfectly struck my intention." He then warned them, saying, "Wang Sanlao from the house next door is used to owing money for meat. Under no circumstances should you extend him credit."

stories.text: 一人死後，轉床殯殮，諸親及眾婦繞靈而哭。只見孝幃裂碎，到處飛揚，皆稱怪象。特往關魂問之，乃曰：「無他，只是當眾人咬嚼不過耳。」
stories.translation: After a man's death, they turned his body and prepared it for burial. All the relatives and women encircled the coffin and wept. Suddenly, they saw the mourning cloth tear into pieces, flying everywhere; everyone called it an ominous phenomenon. They specially went to consult a spirit medium, who said, "Nothing else—just that the deceased couldn't chew through it in front of so many people."

stories.text: 有性吝者，父子在途，每日沽酒一文，慮其易竭，乃約用箸頭蘸嘗之。其子連蘸二次，父責之曰：「如何吃這般急酒！」
stories.translation: There was a man who was very stingy. On the road with his father and son, they bought only one wen of wine each day. Worried that it would run out quickly, they agreed to taste it by dipping the tip of chopsticks into it. The son dipped twice in a row, and his father scolded him, saying, "How can you drink such hurried wine!"

stories.text: 一人好飲，偶赴席，見桌上杯小，遂作嗚咽之狀。主人驚問其故，曰：「睹物傷情耳。先君去世之日，並無疾病，因友人招飲。亦似府上酒杯一般，誤吞入口，咽死了的。今日復見此杯，焉得不哭？」
stories.translation: A man who loved to drink, on a rare occasion attending a banquet, saw that the cups on the table were small and immediately made a weeping face. The host was startled and asked why, to which he replied, "It's just that I'm moved by the sight." "On the day my late father passed away, there was no illness; it was because a friend invited him for a drink." It looked just like this kind of small cup here. He accidentally swallowed it, and choked to death." "I see the same kind of cup today—how could I not cry?"

stories.text: 父子扛酒一壇，路滑跌翻。其父大怒，子乃伏地痛飲，抬頭謂父曰：「決些來麼，難道你還要等甚菜？」
stories.translation: A father and son were carrying a jar of wine when they stumbled and dropped it on the slippery road. The father became very angry, but the son knelt on the ground and drank heartily. Looking up at his father, he said, "Shall I pour some for you? Do you still need to wait for any side dishes?"

stories.text: 客人戀席，不肯起身。主人偶見樹上一大鳥，對客曰：「此席坐久，盤中餚盡，待我砍倒此樹，捉下鳥來，烹與執事侑酒，何如？」客曰：「只恐樹倒鳥飛矣。」主云：「此是呆鳥，他死也不肯動身的。」
stories.translation: A guest lingered at the banquet table, unwilling to leave. The host happened to see a large bird on the tree and said to the guest, "You have been sitting at this banquet for too long; all the dishes are gone. Let me chop down this tree, catch the bird, cook it up, and serve it with wine for you—how does that sound?" The guest said, "I am afraid the bird will fly away once the tree falls." The host replied, "This is a foolish bird; it won't move even when it dies."

stories.text: 一人肩挑磁壺，各處貨賣。行至山間，遇著一虎，咆哮而來。其人愴甚，忙將一壺擲去，其虎不退。再投一壺，虎又不退。投之將盡，止存一壺，乃高聲大喊曰：「畜生，畜生！你若去，也只是這一壺。你就不去，也只是這一壺了！」
stories.translation: A man carried a clay jar on his shoulder and sold it around. While walking through the mountains, he encountered a tiger roaring toward him. The man was greatly frightened and quickly threw one of the jars away, but the tiger did not retreat. He threw another jar, yet the tiger still did not back off. When he had thrown almost all of them and only one jar remained, he shouted loudly, "Beast! Beast!" "If you go away now, it will be just this one jar." "And if you don't go, it's still going to be only this one jar!"

stories.text: 一人貪飲過度，妻子私相謀議曰：「屢勸不聽，宜以險事動之。」一日，大飲而噦，子密袖豬膈置噦中，指以謂曰：「凡人具五臟，今出一臟矣，何以生耶？」父熟視曰：「唐三藏尚活世，況我有四臟乎！」
stories.translation: A man drank excessively, and his wife secretly discussed with him, saying, "We have advised him many times but he would not listen. We should use a dangerous situation to shock him." loin One day, while he was drinking heavily and vomiting, his son secretly slipped a piece of pork diaphragm into the vomit. Pointing at it, he said to him, "Every person has five zang organs; now one organ is missing. How can you live?" The father looked at it carefully and said, "Tang Sanzang is still alive in the world; if he can live with only four zang organs, then I have four as well!"

stories.text: 一人以寡酒勸客，客曰：「不如拿把刀來殺了我罷。」主愕然，問曰：「勸酒無非好意，何出此言？」客曰：「其實當你寡不過了。」
stories.translation: A man offered wine to a guest, who said, "It would be better if you just brought out a knife and killed me." The host was startled and asked, "Offering wine is always meant with good intentions. Why do you say such a thing?" The guest said, "It's just that your wine has become too poor for me."

stories.text: 夜遊神見門神夜立，憐而問之曰：「汝長大乃爾，如何做人門客，早晚伺候，受此苦辛？」門神曰：「出於無奈耳。」曰：「然則有飯吃否？」答：「若要他飯吃時，又不要我上門了。」
stories.translation: The Night Roaming Deity saw the Door Gods standing at night and, feeling pity for them, asked, "You have grown so tall. How could you become a door guardian, waiting day and night, enduring such hardship?" The Door God replied, "It's out of necessity." He asked, "Then do you at least get to eat?" The answer was, "If they want me to eat, then they no longer need a door guardian."

stories.text: 一人夢赴戲酌，方定席，為妻驚醒，乃罵其妻。妻曰：「不要罵，趁早睡去，戲文還未半本哩。」
stories.translation: A man dreamed of attending a drinking gathering. Just as he was about to sit down, his wife woke him up and he scolded her. The wife said, "Don't scold me. Go to sleep early; the play is not even halfway through yet."

stories.text: 一好飲者，夢得美酒。將熱而飲之，忽被驚醒，乃大悔曰：「早知如此，恨不冷吃。」
stories.translation: A wine lover dreamed that he had obtained fine wine. Just as he was about to warm it up and drink, he suddenly woke up from a start. He regretted greatly and said, "If I had known this would happen, I wish I could have drunk it cold."

stories.text: 使僮斟酒不滿，客舉盃細視良久，曰：「此盃太深，當截去一段。」主曰：「為何？」客曰：「上半段盛不得酒，要他何用？」
stories.translation: A servant poured wine into a cup but did not fill it completely. The guest held up the cup and examined it carefully for a long time, then said, "This cup is too deep; I should cut off a section of it." The host asked, "Why?" The guest replied, "The upper half cannot hold wine. What use is it to me?"

stories.text: 主有留客定飯，僅用切肉一碗，既囂且少。乃作詩以誚之，曰：「君家之刀利且鋒，君家之手輕且鬆。切來片片如紙同，周圍披轉無二重。推窗忽遇微小風，頓然吹入五雲中。忙忙令人覓其蹤，已過巫山十二峰。」
stories.translation: The host had prepared a meal to entertain his guest, serving only one bowl of thinly sliced meat, which was both unimpressive and meager. He composed a poem to mock him, saying: "Your knife is sharp and keen, your hand light and loose. Each slice you cut is as thin as paper; it turns around the edges without a second layer." Pushing open the window, he suddenly encountered a slight breeze that blew him into the Five Clouds above. "In great haste I sent someone to search for its trace, but it had already passed over twelve peaks of Wushan."

stories.text: 客見坐上無餚，乃作意謝主人，稱其大費。主人曰：「一些菜也沒有，何云大費？」客曰：「滿盤都是。」主人曰：「菜在那裡？」客指盤中曰：「這不是菜，難道到是肉不成？」
stories.translation: The guest, seeing no dishes on the table, pretended to thank the host and praised his great expense. The host said, "There isn't even a single dish; how can you say it's expensive?" The guest replied, "It is all over the plate." The host asked, "Where are the dishes?" The guest pointed to the plate and said, "This is not a dish? Could it be meat instead?"

stories.text: 一家延師，供膳菲薄。時值天雨，館僮攜午膳至，肉甚少，師以其來遲，欲責之。僮曰：「天雨路滑故也。」師曰：「汝可寫滑字我看，如寫得出，便饒你打。」僮曰：「一點兒，一點兒，又是斜披一點兒，其餘都是骨了。」
stories.translation: A family hired a teacher, but provided meager meals. At the time it was raining, and when the servant brought lunch to the teacher's quarters, there was very little meat. The teacher wanted to scold him for arriving late. The servant said, "It is because of the rainy and slippery road." The teacher said, "You can write the character 'hua' for me to see. If you can write it correctly, I will spare you a beating." The servant said, "A dot, another dot, and then another slanted dot; the rest is just bones."

stories.text: 一母命子攜蘿蔔一籃，往河邊洗滌。久之不歸，母往尋之，但存蘿蔔。知兒失足墮河，淹死水中，因大哭曰：「我的肉，我的肉，但見蘿蔔不見肉。」
stories.translation: A mother ordered her son to carry a basket of radishes and go to the riverbank to wash them. After some time, he did not return. The mother went to look for him but found only the radishes left behind. Knowing that her son had lost his footing and fallen into the river, drowning in it, she wept bitterly and said, "My flesh and blood, my flesh and blood—only radishes are here; I see no meat."

stories.text: 有請客者，盤飧少而和頭多，因嘲之曰：「府上的食品，忒煞富貴相了。」主問：「何以見得？」曰：「蔥蒜蘿蔔，都用魚肉片子來拌的。少刻魚肉上來，一定是龍肝鳳髓做和頭了。」
stories.translation: A host invited guests, but the dishes were few while there were many bowls of porridge. Someone mocked him and said, "Your food is far too luxurious." The host asked, "How can you say that?" He replied, "Scallions, garlic, and radishes are all mixed with slices of fish and meat." 龙头 In a moment, when the fish and meat were served, they must have used dragon liver and phoenix marrow for the porridge topping.

stories.text: 一家請客，骨多肉少。客曰：「府上的碗想是偷來的？」主人駭曰：「何出此言？」客曰：「我只聽見人家罵說：『偷我的碗，拿去盛骨頭。』」
stories.translation: A family hosted a banquet, but there were more bones and less meat. The guest said, "Are your bowls stolen?" The host was startled and asked, "Why do you say that?" The guest replied, "I only heard people cursing: 'Steal my bowls and use them to hold bones.'"

stories.text: 館僮怪主人每食必盡，只留光骨於碗，乃對天祝曰：「願相公活一百歲，小的活一百零一歲。」主問其故，答曰：「小人多活一歲，好收拾相公的骨頭。」
stories.translation: The servant in the teacher's quarters was puzzled that his master always ate everything, leaving only bare bones in the bowl. So he prayed to heaven and said, "May my master live for a hundred years, and I, just one year longer." The host asked why he said that. The servant replied, "If I live one more year, it will be good for collecting my master's bones."

stories.text: 或有宴會，座中客貪饞不已，餚使既盡。館僮憤怒而不敢言，乃以鍋煤塗滿嘴上，站立傍側。眾人見而訝之，問其嘴間何物。答曰：「相公們只顧自己吃罷了，別人的嘴管他則甚。」
stories.translation: At a banquet, there were guests who kept eating greedily until all the dishes had been finished. The servant in charge of the banquet was angry but dared not speak, so he smeared his mouth with soot and stood by. Everyone saw this and was surprised, asking what substance was on his mouth. He replied, "My masters only care about eating themselves; why should they care about someone else's mouth?"

stories.text: 有與善啖者同席，見盤中且盡，呼主翁拿燭來。主曰：「得無太早乎？」曰：「我桌上已一些不見了。」
stories.translation: Someone dined with an excellent eater and, seeing the dishes nearly finished, called out to the host for a candle. The host asked, "Isn't it too early?" He replied, "There is nothing left on my table."

stories.text: 一家請客，失分一箸。上菜之後，眾客朝拱舉箸，其人獨抻手而觀。徐向主人曰：「求賜清水一碗。」主問曰：「何處用之？」答曰：「洗乾淨了指頭，好拈菜吃。」
stories.translation: A family hosted a banquet and lost one chopstick. lodash After the dishes were served, all the guests bowed politely and picked up their chopsticks, but this man alone stretched out his hand to look on. He slowly approached the host and said, "May I request a bowl of clear water?" The host asked, "Where will you use it?" He replied, "I want to wash my fingers clean so I can pick up the food and eat."

stories.text: 有作客異鄉者，每入席，輒狂啖不已。同席之人甚惡之，因問曰：「貴處每逢月食，如何護法？」答曰：「官府穿公服群聚，率軍校侍兵擊鼓為對，俟其吐出始散。」其人亦問同席者曰：「貴鄉同否？」答曰：「敝處不然，只是善求。」問：「如何求法？」曰：「合掌了手，對黑月說道：『阿彌陀佛，脫煞凶了，求你省可吃些，剩點與人看看罷。』」
stories.translation: A guest in a foreign land, whenever he sat down to a banquet, would eat greedily without stopping. The other guests at the table were very annoyed and asked him, "In your hometown, how do you protect the law during a lunar eclipse?" He replied, "The government officials wear official robes and gather in groups. They lead military schools and soldiers to beat drums as a response, waiting until it spits out before dispersing." The man also asked the other guest, "Is your hometown any different?" He replied, "Not in my hometown. We just ask for more." The man asked, "How do you ask?" He said, "Clasp your hands together and say to the dark moon: 'Amituofo, you have already devoured too much. I beg of you to spare some for others to see.'"

stories.text: 甲好啖，手不停箸，問乙曰：「兄如何箸也不動？」乙還問曰：「兄如何動也不住？」
stories.translation: Jia loved to eat and never stopped picking up his chopsticks. He asked Yi, "Brother, why are you not even moving your chopsticks?" Yi replied with a question, "Brother, how come you can't stop moving them at all?"

stories.text: 有客饞甚，每入座，輒餮饕不已。一日，與之同席，自言曾會過一次，友曰：「並未謀面，想是老兄錯認了。」及上菜後，啖者低頭大嚼，雙箸不停。彼人大悟，曰：「是了，會便會過一次，因兄只顧吃菜，終席不曾抬頭，所以認不得尊容，莫怪莫怪。」
stories.translation: There was a guest who was extremely greedy. Every time he sat down, he would eat greedily without restraint. One day, while dining with him, the guest claimed they had met once before. His companion said, "We have never met; I think you've mistaken me for someone else, my elder brother." After the dishes were served, the gluttonous guest lowered his head and began to eat heartily, never stopping with his chopsticks. The other person suddenly realized and said, "Ah, yes! We did meet once before. It was because you were too absorbed in eating and never looked up throughout the meal, so I couldn't recognize your face. Please don't be offended."

stories.text: 一酒客訝同席者飲啖太猛，問其年，以屬犬對。客曰：「早是犬，若屬虎的，連我也都吃下肚了。」
stories.translation: A drinking guest was surprised that his fellow diner ate and drank so voraciously, and asked for his birth year. The man replied that he belonged to the Dog zodiac sign. The guest said, "Even as a Dog, you're already so ravenous; if you were a Tiger, you would have eaten me up too."

stories.text: 一人與瞽者同席，先上東坡肉一碗，瞽者舉箸即拑而啖之。同席者惡甚。少焉復來撈取，盤中已空如也。問曰：「肉有幾塊？」其人憤然答曰：「九塊。」瞽者曰：「你倒吃了八塊麼。」
stories.translation: A man dined with a blind person. A bowl of Dongpo pork was served first, and the blind man picked it up immediately with his chopsticks and devoured it. The fellow guest was very annoyed. After a short while, the blind man came back to take more, but the plate was already empty. He asked, "How many pieces of meat were there?" The man angrily replied, "Nine pieces." The blind man said, "Then you must have eaten eight of them."

stories.text: 兩人共席而飲，碗內有黃雀四隻，一人貪食其三，謂同席者曰：「兄何不用？」其人曰：「索性放在兄腹中，省得他們拆了對？」
stories.translation: Two men were drinking together at the same table. There were four yellow sparrows in a bowl, and one of them greedily ate three of them. He said to his fellow guest, "Brother, why don't you eat any?" The other man replied, "Just put them in your stomach altogether; it will save the trouble of them being split up."

stories.text: 一妻病，夫問曰：「想甚吃否？」妻曰：「除非好肉餛飩，想吃一二隻。」夫為治一盂，意欲與妻同享，方往取箸回，而妻已染指啖盡，止餘其一。夫曰：「何不并啖此枚？」妻攢眉曰：「我若吃得下此隻，不害這病了。」
stories.translation: A wife was ill, and her husband asked, "Do you feel like eating anything?" The wife said, "Unless it's good meat-filled wontons; I would like to eat one or two." The husband prepared a bowl, intending to share it with his wife. When he went to get the chopsticks and returned, the wife had already dipped her fingers in and eaten all but one. The husband said, "Why not eat this last one as well?" The wife frowned and said, "If I could eat this one, I wouldn't be sick in the first place."

stories.title_en: Punishing by Turning into a Crab
stories.text: 一人見冥王，自陳一生吃素，要求個好輪回。王曰：「我那裡查考，須剖腹驗之。」既剖，但見一肚饞涎。因曰：「罰你去變一隻蟹，依舊吐出了罷。」
stories.translation: A man appeared before the King of Hell and declared that he had eaten vegetarian food all his life, requesting a good reincarnation. The king said, "I need to check for myself; I must open your abdomen and examine it." After the examination, they found only a belly full of drooling greed. They said, "Punish you to be reborn as a crab and continue spitting it out."

stories.text: 一人遇餓虎，將遭啖。其人哀懇曰：「圈有肥豬，願將代己。」虎許之，隨至其家。喚婦取豬喂虎，婦不捨曰：「所有豆腐頗多，亦堪一飽。」夫曰：「罷麼，你看這樣一個狠主客，可是肯吃素的麼？」
stories.translation: A man encountered a starving tiger and was about to be devoured. The man pleaded desperately, "There is a fat pig in the pen; I beg you to let it take my place instead." The tiger agreed and followed him to his home. He called his wife to bring the pig for the tiger, but she was reluctant and said, "We have plenty of tofu; it should be enough to satisfy him." The husband replied, "Well then, do you think such a cruel guest would agree to eat vegetarian food?"

stories.text: 有以淡酒宴客者，客嘗之，極贊府上烹調之美。主曰：「粗餚未曾上桌，何以見得？」答曰：「不必論其他，只這一味酒煮白滾湯，就妙起了。」
stories.translation: A host served guests with thin wine. After tasting it, the guest highly praised the excellence of the cooking at his home. The host said, "We haven't even served the simple dishes yet; how could you know that?" He replied, "There's no need to talk about anything else. Just this one dish of wine-boiled clear soup is already excellent."

stories.text: 有人宴客用淡酒者，客向主人索刀。主問曰：「要他何用？」曰：「欲殺此壺。」又問：「壺何可殺？」答曰：「殺了他，解解水氣。」
stories.translation: A man hosted a banquet using thin wine, and the guest asked the host for a knife. The host asked, "What do you need it for?" He said, "I want to kill this wine jar." The host asked again, "Why would you want to kill a wine jar?" He replied, "Killing it will help dispel the watery taste."

stories.text: 河魚與海魚攀親，河魚屢往，備擾海錯。因語海魚：「親家，何不到小去處下顧一顧？」海魚許焉。河魚歸曰：「海頭太太至矣。」遣手下擇深港迎之。海魚甫至港口便返，河魚追問其故，答曰：「我吃不慣貴處這樣淡水。」
stories.translation: A river fish wanted to be related to a sea fish, and the river fish visited repeatedly, disturbing the sea creatures. The sea fish said to him, "Relative-in-law, why don't you come visit my humble place?" The sea fish agreed. The river fish returned and said, "The lady of the sea has arrived." He sent his subordinates to choose a deep harbor to welcome her. As soon as the sea fish arrived at the harbor, she turned back. The river fish chased after her and asked why, to which she replied, "I'm not used to your place's fresh water."

stories.text: 一家請客，酒甚淡。客曰：「餚饌只此足矣，倒是米求得一撮出來。」主曰：「要他何用？」答曰：「此酒想是不曾下得米，倒要放幾顆。」
stories.translation: A family hosted a banquet, and the wine was very thin. The guest said, "The dishes are sufficient as they are; what I really need is just a handful of rice." The host asked, "What do you need it for?" He replied, "This wine must not have had any rice in it; I want to add a few grains."

stories.text: 一人請客，客方舉杯，即放聲大哭。主人慌問曰：「臨飲何故而悲？」答曰：「我生平最愛的是酒，今酒已死矣，因此而哭。」主笑曰：「酒如何得死？」客曰：「既不曾死，如何沒有一些酒氣？」
stories.translation: A man hosted guests, and as the guest was about to raise his cup, he suddenly burst into loud weeping. The host panicked and asked, "Why are you so sad just before drinking?" He replied, "I love wine the most in my life. Now it is already dead; that's why I'm crying." The host laughed and said, "How could the wine possibly die?" The guest replied, "If it hasn't died, how come there is not even a hint of alcohol in it?"

stories.title_en: Presenting You as Substitute for Wine
stories.text: 一客訪客，主人不留飲食，起送出門，謂客曰：「古語云：『遠送當三杯』，待我送君里許。」恐客留滯，急拽其袖而行。客曰：「求從容些，量淺，吃不得這般急酒。」
stories.translation: A guest visited another guest, but the host did not offer food or drink and immediately stood up to see him out. He said to the visitor, "An old saying goes: 'Seeing a distant guest off is like offering three cups of wine.' Let me walk with you for several li." Afraid the guest might linger, he hurriedly pulled his sleeve and walked. The guest said, "Please go a bit more slowly; I'm not used to drinking this fast."
